title: Token Heatmap Reconciler — concept notes and wireframe backlog
body:
Purpose
----
Quick working doc to collect UX ideas for a "heatmap reconciler" view: a dashboard panel that surfaces token-level cost and latency anomalies and ties them back to invocation fingerprints, prompt sections, and runtime events (cache hits, batching, fallbacks). Goal is to make it easy for engineers/product owners to reconcile observed billable tokens with perceived latencies and debug weird cost spikes.

Primary user stories / jobs-to-be-done
----
- As an ML infra engineer, I want to see which part of a prompt produced the majority of billable tokens so I can tune truncation/templating.
- As a product PM, I want an at-a-glance visualization that surfaces top invocations by cost per minute so I can prioritize rollout/optimizations.
- As an SRE, I want to quickly map latency outliers to runtime events (model fallback, quantization variant, long KV cache fill) and jump to traces.

Core ideas (non-final)
----
1) Heatmap-grid: rows = invocation fingerprints (hash of prompt + settings), columns = token position buckets (0–20, 21–100, 101–512, 513+). Cell color = cost density (tokens * per-token-weight) or median latency contribution. Hover shows sample prompt snippet for that bucket and top 3 invocations contributing.

2) Reconciler strip: below heatmap, a horizontal "reconciliation strip" where we show three stacked bars per invocation: billed tokens, cached tokens (invisible billing), and effective latency. Allows quick visual mismatches (large billed tokens but low latency suggests batching or long-lived KV reuse; large latency but low billed tokens suggests model cold start or backend queue).

3) Timeline slider + streaming-aware playback: for a selected invocation fingerprint, the timeline replays token production in streaming mode, highlighting when cache hits occurred and when fallback to lower tier/region happened. Useful for debugging partial-stream issues.

4) Attribution drilldown: clicking a cell opens a side panel with: canonical prompt text (with masked user data), token-by-token cost and token-by-token latency (median, p90), a short list of correlated runtime events (fallbacks, retries, variant selection), and links to related traces/logs. Provide a one-click copy of the prompt section (sanitized) for quick repro.

5) Data stitching rules (important): we surface attributed token costs only when we can link a request trace to a billing record within a 30s window AND model variant matches. If no match, mark as "unreconciled" and push to a queue for batched reconciliation. Need to show confidence score per row.

Wireframe notes (element-level)
----
- Header: fingerprint short id + human-friendly alias (auto-generated from prompt template). Small chevron to expand metadata (region, model, quantization profile, edge-case tags).
- Left column: fingerprint list, with sparkline for cost-per-minute and latency p95. Ability to pin favorites.
- Main: heatmap grid (SVG), with row labels truncated after 40 chars. Legend to switch metric between cost-density, latency-contribution, and token-count.
- Bottom: reconciliation strip + small table of top 5 contributing requests (timestamp, user org, billed tokens, latency ms, trace id link).
- Right panel (scratchpad): attribution details and action buttons (open trace, export prompt, create ticket, create snapshot).

Interaction details / microcopy
----
- Hover cell: "~3.2k billed tokens, median latency 140ms — click to inspect"
- Unreconciled badge: tooltip: "We could not match these invocations to billing records (likely async batching or delayed billing). Click to queue for deeper reconcile."
- Confidence indicator: small pill with green/yellow/red and short text: "High confidence (billing link found)" or "Low (approximate match by model+time)"

Edge cases & tricky signals
----
- Streaming partials: when clients reconnect mid-stream, token attribution may split across multiple request IDs. Need heuristics to re-associate by contiguous KV cache keys and user-session id.
- Retries and duplicates: distinguish retries (same request id) vs duplicate content (different request ids same prompt) to avoid double-counting.
- Function/tool-calls: tokens consumed by external tool invocation vs model. Show tool token bucket separately and allow toggling inclusion in billed totals.
- Sub-tokenization quirks across model families (some models count tokens slightly differently). Add "model token mapping" note per fingerprint when mismatch suspected.

Mock data example (for wireframe)
----
rows: ["checkout-summary-v1", "search-query-embed", "agent-chain-step-3"]
columns: [0-20, 21-100, 101-512, 513+]
cell (checkout-summary-v1, 21-100) = {
  "sample_prompts": ["order summary: {{items}}..."],
  "billed_tokens": "1,642",
  "median_latency_ms": "78",
  "confidence": "high"
}
(We will render the above as flattened cells in the UI; this doc keeps it readable for designers.)

Backlog / actionable tickets (candidate priorities)
----
- [P0] RDW-2110: "Reconciliation API: join trace events and billing records" (blocking heatmap accuracy).
- [P0] RDW-2185: "Heatmap SVG generator + client-side zoom/pan". UX needs smooth pan for hundreds of rows.
- [P1] RDW-2231: "Streaming playback UX: step controls + cache hit markers".
- [P1] RDW-2256: "Unreconciled queue UX + manual reconcile flow".
- [P2] RDW-2299: "Model token mapping table + per-model adjustments".

Acceptance criteria (for an initial MVP)
----
- MVP shows top 50 invocation fingerprints in last 24h with heatmap and reconciliation strip.
- Clicking any heatmap cell opens the right panel with token and latency breakdown, and at least one linked trace (if confidence is high).
- Unreconciled rows clearly identified and link to queue.
- Desktop layout responsive to 1200px width; SVG interactions <150ms for common actions.

Open questions / decisions to make
----
- When switching between metrics (cost vs latency), should color scale be independent per-row or global across the grid? Pros/cons: per-row highlights local peaks, global helps cross-row comparison. Leaning global for PM use-cases, add per-row toggle.
- Should we auto-generate aliases for fingerprints or require teams to register templates? Hybrid: generate, allow manual override + team annotations.
- Privacy: how much prompt text do we show in hover/sample? Need clear privacy-preserving defaults and quick redaction button. Ask security/compliance.

Design notes for dev handoff
----
- Provide a small example dataset with 50 rows and canonical schema: fingerprint, alias, timestamps[], cell_metrics[] (flattened strings acceptable for prototype).
- Export formats: CSV/JSON and an "export snapshot" (tar of associated traces + minimal anonymized prompt) for handoff to infra teams.
- Accessibility: keyboard-only navigation across heatmap cells, ARIA labels for color legend, and high-contrast color palette option.

Next steps (this week)
----
- Sync with Diego (infra) to finalize reconciliation window and confidence heuristics — RDW-2110 sync Wed 10am.
- Designer sketch pass: Rina to produce 3 compact alternatives (grid density vs list-focus) by Thu.
- Engineering spike: prototype heatmap rendering with static mock data (PR #432) — target EOD Fri.

Notes to self / scratch ideas
----
- Consider small inline cost-saver tips per fingerprint: e.g., "Replace static <=20 items listing with summary token-saver". Could be AI-suggested prompt edits.
- Think about a "cost forecast" overlay using recent slope to predict next 24h spend for pinned fingerprints.

References & inspiration
----
- Datadog flamegraphs and heatmap interactions (good examples for zoom behavior).
- Billing reconciliation runbook (confluence: token-attribution-runbook)
- Internal trace format docs: infra/tracing/trace-schema.md

END
